title: The Effect of Sleep on Tendon Cellular Adaptation
official: The Effect of Sleep on Human Tendon Cellular Remodeling: a ex Vivo Pilot Study.
summary:
The goal of this observational study is to evaluate the effect of hormones which surge or diminish during different stages of sleep on collagen turnover in tendon cells. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. To evaluate the effect of serum taken from participants overnight on human tendon cell-derived collagen expression in a cell culture model.
2. To evaluate whether tendon cell-derived collagen expression in a cell culture model is driven by changes in collagen synthesis or breakdown.

To evaluate the effect of sleep on tendon adaptation, blood will be taken from human participants overnight and used to treat a tendon cell culture model.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* healthy (determined using a medical screening questionnaire)
* between the ages of 18 and 35
* participants must be a non-smoker
* self-reported moderately active (\>150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per week)
* self-reported weight stable (\< 2 kg increase or decrease in weight over the previous 6 months)
* sleep ≥ 7 hours per night
* female participants must have a stable menstrual cycle (\>3 months of 21-35 day cycle length).

Exclusion Criteria:

* have a BMI \<18.5 or \>29.9 kg/m2
* have a history of clinically diagnosed insomnia (\>7 on the Insomnia Severity Index) or other sleep disorder (e.g., sleep apnea)
* use a hormonal contraceptive (oral or IUD)
* consume 7+ standard drinks per week (high risk range)
* use cannabis \>1 time per week
* have any concurrent medical, orthopedic, or psychiatric condition that, in the opinion of the investigators, would compromise the ability to comply with the study requirements
* regularly use anti-inflammatory and/or analgesic medication, whether prescription or not; use any medications known to affect collagen metabolism (e.g., glucocorticoids, acetaminophen, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medication, or prescription strength acne medication, ACE inhibitors, proton pump inhibitors, growth hormone, GLP-1 receptor agonists);
* participated in a study involving a phenylalanine stable-isotope tracer in the previous year
